Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) are trading higher early Wednesday after Reuters reported the chipmaker is in talks with a Korean memory partner about producing memory chips at Intel's Ohio campus. Intel stock is up 4% to $100.55 in early Wednesday trading, extending a run that has the shares up 171% year to date. The move points to a paying tenant on the same site Intel has been funding on its own.

JasonDoiy / iStock Unreleased via Getty Images

SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) is the reported counterparty, and its U.S.-listed shares are climbing on the same story. SK Hynix stock is up 3.3% to $180.52. The Korean memory leader is in the middle of a wider U.S. build-out that already includes a groundbreaking last month on a high-bandwidth memory (HBM) production base in Indiana.

The read-through is more complicated for Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), the leading U.S.-based memory supplier, whose shares are barely moving on the news. Micron stock is up 0.9% to $935.80 as the market weighs whether a Korean rival producing on American soil would erode Micron's home-market advantage under the CHIPS Act.

title: Wells Fargo Resets S&P 500 Target With a Catch
detail:
Wells Fargo Resets S&P 500 Target With a Catch
Moz Farooque ACCA
Tue, September 15, 2026 at 4:19 PM EDT 2 min read
WFC
^GSPC
QQQ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Wells Fargo has cut its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,700 from 7,950, warning that investors are entering the late stages of the market's growth cycle just as political risks and pressure on technology stocks complicate the outlook. The revised target implies only about 1% upside from the index's recent 7,619.98 close, signaling that the bank sees limited room for further gains through the rest of 2026 despite strong corporate earnings.

Is QQQ fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The S&P 500 has still gained 11.3% this year, weathering Middle East tensions, sticky inflation and periodic volatility.

Corporate fundamentals also remain resilient. Roughly 85.7% of S&P 500 companies reporting second-quarter results beat Wall Street earnings estimates.

Wells Fargo is not turning outright bearish on profits. The bank actually raised its S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecast to $425 for 2027 and $460 for 2028.

The concern is what investors will be willing to pay for those earnings.

Wells Fargo said the market is moving deeper into a late-cycle environment, where valuation multiples typically compress and price gains become harder to generate. The bank also warned that its 2028 earnings forecast could prove too optimistic if major technology companies pull back on massive AI infrastructure spending.

That risk is already changing its sector positioning.

Wells Fargo downgraded U.S. technology stocks to equal weight from overweight following Monday's AI-led selloff and rising political pushback against large data-center developments ahead of the midterm elections.

At the same time, the bank upgraded healthcare to overweight from equal weight as a more defensive late-cycle opportunity.

Investors Takeaway

Wells Fargo's call suggests the next leg of the market may depend less on earnings growth and more on valuation.

Investors should watch AI capital spending, tech earnings revisions and whether political pressure begins delaying data-center projects. A sustained slowdown in hyperscaler spending would threaten both tech valuations and Wells Fargo's longer-term earnings assumptions.

Conversely, continued strong earnings combined with resilient AI investment could make the 7,700 target look conservative. For now, Wells Fargo's shift toward healthcare signals a preference for earnings durability over chasing further tech multiple expansion.

Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) shares are climbing sharply Tuesday morning, and the move stands out because the broader large-cap technology group is slipping at the same time. Skyworks stock is up 11% to $87.68, the sharpest jump among the handset chip names. That gain builds on a year that was already strong, with Skyworks stock up 41% year to date.

HelloRF Zcool / Shutterstock.com

Qorvo (NASDAQ:QRVO) stock is also rallying, rising 7% to $116.02, tracking its merger partner higher. Meanwhile, Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) stock is up 4% to $187.72, the largest of the three names and, as often happens when a theme is being bought aggressively at the smaller end, the smallest mover of the group.

The sector benchmark is barely participating. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up just 0.5% to $499.74, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 0.5% to $705.50. That split, with three handset-levered chip names ripping while the broader semiconductor fund and the large-cap tech proxy do nothing, is the shape of today's trade.

Rotation Into Handset Chip Names

No company announcement from Skyworks, Qorvo or Qualcomm accounts for moves of this size in a single session. These are radio frequency (RF) front-end and analog names, and they trade on smartphone unit volumes, dollar content per handset, and industrial and automotive demand rather than on artificial intelligence data center capital spending. That's why Skyworks and its peers routinely move independently of the AI chip names inside the same session, and why the semiconductor fund barely moving while three of its handset-levered constituents rally is the expected structure rather than a contradiction.
